transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, thank you so much for seeing me. Um, well, I guess I'm just here because... well, I've been having a little trouble at work lately. I mean, I'm an advertising sales agent, so it's a lot of meetings, and I love my job, I really do! But... I've noticed, and I guess some other people have noticed, that I have a hard time just... staying in my chair during those really long strategy meetings. 

I know I'm supposed to stay seated, but I just find myself getting up a lot. You know, just to grab some water, or I'll kind of pace over by the printer for a minute. It's not a huge deal, I don't think, but it's starting to feel a little embarrassing. Is that... does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm doing a good job and not being disruptive, you know?
Do you find yourself feeling restless or needing to move around in other situations, like at home or in social settings, or is this something that only happens during those long work meetings?

Oh, um... I don't really think so? I mean, I haven't really noticed it happening at home or, like, when I'm out with friends. At home, I'm usually just, you know, tidying up or getting things done around the apartment, so being on my feet is pretty normal, right? And socially, we're usually out and about anyway, so it's not like I'm forced to sit perfectly still. 

So I think it's really just those super long work meetings where you're kind of trapped at a conference table. I hope that's a good thing? Like, I'm really not trying to make a huge deal out of it, I just want to make sure I'm doing things right and being a good employee.
Have you noticed that this kind of restlessness or need to move around has been a pattern for you going back to when you were younger, like in school or when you were a teenager?

Um... well, if I really think about it... I guess, yeah, it might go back a bit further? Like, even way before high school. I feel a little silly admitting this, but... my elementary school teachers, they were always really nice, and they'd write on my report cards that I was a bright student—which is a good thing, right? 

But... they also usually added that I rushed through my work a lot. And, um, maybe that I talked out of turn sometimes. I also had a bit of a bad habit of forgetting my homework, and... my desk was always just stuffed with all these half-finished papers. I mean, kids are just messy sometimes, aren't they? I really did try to be a good student, I promise, it's just... I guess I was a little scattered back then. Is that... does that answer your question okay?
As a child, did you have trouble staying seated or focusing during activities, even outside of school, like at home or during family meals?

Um... no, not really. I mean, at home, things were pretty relaxed, you know? I don't remember my parents ever getting upset with me for not sitting still at dinner or anything like that. We usually just ate and chatted, and it was fine. And if I was playing or doing something I liked, I was totally fine just doing that. 

I think... I think I was a pretty normal kid at home, honestly. I always tried to be good for my parents. I hope that's what you were asking? I just don't want to make it sound like I was this out-of-control kid everywhere I went, because I really wasn't.
Do you find it hard to focus on tasks at work, especially during those long meetings, or do you feel easily distracted by things around you?

Um... well, I always try really hard to stay on top of things, because my job and my clients are super important to me. But... I guess, yeah, sometimes it can be a little tricky? 

Like, if we're in one of those longer strategy meetings, or if I'm reading through a really big client brief... I always start out completely focused and ready to go. But then, after a few minutes, I'll kind of snap back and realize I've just been staring at the exact same slide, or the same paragraph, and I have absolutely no idea what the last point even was. 

I mean, everyone zones out a little bit when there's a ton of information to process, right? I really hope that doesn't make me sound like I'm slacking off or not paying attention on purpose, because I really do care about doing a good job. Is that... does that make sense?
Outside of work, do you find it hard to stay focused on things like reading, watching TV, or following conversations with friends or family?

Um... outside of work? No, I don't think so. I mean, I really value my relationships, so when I'm with my friends or family, I always make sure to listen to what they're saying. I'd never want them to feel like I don't care about what's going on in their lives. 

And with reading or TV... I mean, I guess if a show is just really boring, I might check my phone or something, but that's pretty normal, right? Everyone multitasks nowadays. If it's something I'm actually interested in, I have no problem watching it. I really try to be present when I'm spending time with people or relaxing. I hope that's the kind of answer you were looking for?
Can you describe a typical workday for me? Specifically, how easy or difficult is it for you to organize your tasks, manage your time, and stay focused from morning until the end of the day?

Um... a typical workday. Well, I always want to make sure I'm doing a really good job for my clients, so I try my best to keep everything on track. I mean, advertising sales is pretty fast-paced, so there's always a lot going on. 

I guess... well, sometimes getting everything organized can be a little... challenging? But I'm sure everybody feels that way sometimes, right? It's just that... well, when I'm working on a campaign, I'll take notes in an email, and then maybe I'll jot something down on a sticky note while I'm on a call, and then I'll put something else in my actual planner... and I usually have a bunch of tabs open on my computer, too. 

So, I guess sometimes I end up spending a bit more time than I should just trying to figure out where all my notes are and what I'm supposed to actually do first, instead of just... starting the work. But I really do get it all done! I just... I might take the long way around sometimes. I hope that doesn't make me sound completely disorganized? I really do try to keep it all together.

Outside of the meetings at work, have you noticed that this restlessness or difficulty staying focused affects other important parts of your life, like your personal relationships or your ability to relax at home?

Um... well, outside of work, I think things are mostly okay. I really try to be present with my friends and family, like I said. But... um... I guess where it's really starting to become an issue is actually back at work, if I'm being completely honest. 

I really didn't want to bring this up because I don't want it to sound like I'm bad at my job, because I really, really care about my clients. But... um... it's kind of started showing up in my performance reviews lately? Just little comments about my attention to detail. And... well, there was this one time recently where a client actually complained. 

It was just a misunderstanding, I think, but it really scared me. I just... I worry so much that I might accidentally damage one of my accounts, even though I'm trying so hard to do everything right. I just want to do good work for them, you know? I hope you don't think I'm irresponsible... I really am trying my best to keep everything running smoothly. Does that make sense?

Can you tell me if the difficulties you're experiencing with staying focused and feeling restless have ever caused problems in any areas of your life outside of work, such as with your personal relationships, household responsibilities, or other daily activities at home?

Um... outside of work? No, I really don't think so. I mean, I try really hard to keep my personal life running smoothly. I know I mentioned that work has been a little stressful lately, but at home... um... things are pretty normal. 

I make sure to keep up with my chores and everything. Sometimes I might leave a basket of laundry out for a day or two, or maybe I'll start cleaning the kitchen and then get sidetracked by organizing the mail... but that's just normal, right? Everyone gets a little distracted at home when they're trying to relax after a long day. 

And with my relationships, like I said before, I really value my friends and family. I would never let my work stress or anything else get in the way of being there for them. I always try to be a good friend and a good partner. I hope that's what you were asking? I just really want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Have you noticed any days recently where you felt down, sad, or uninterested in things you usually enjoy?

Um... down or sad? No, not really. I mean, I have my moments where I feel a little overwhelmed with everything at work, like I mentioned, but I wouldn't say I feel sad or... or depressed or anything like that. 

I'm actually a pretty upbeat person! I always try to look on the bright side of things, and I still really enjoy my hobbies when I have the time for them. I like to keep a positive attitude, especially for my clients and my friends. I hope that's a good thing? I just... I don't want you to think I'm sitting around feeling sorry for myself, because I'm definitely not. Does that sound okay?
Do you ever feel down, frustrated, or discouraged specifically after work, especially on days when things didn't go as planned or you felt particularly distracted?

Um... frustrated after work? Well, I mean, I think everyone has days where they feel a little discouraged if things don't go perfectly, right? But... um... I wouldn't say I get really down or anything. 

Sometimes if I've had a day where I was a bit... all over the place with my accounts, I might feel a tiny bit annoyed with myself on the drive home. Just because I want to do such a good job for everyone. But it's really just a passing thing! I usually just turn on some upbeat music and remind myself that tomorrow is a fresh start. I really try not to bring any negativity home with me. I hope that makes sense? I just always try to focus on doing better next time rather than getting upset. Is that a normal way to handle it?
Have you noticed any recent changes in your energy levels, like feeling unusually tired or having trouble getting motivated, even when you’re not physically exhausted?

Um... unusually tired? No, I really don't think so. I mean, my energy levels feel pretty normal to me. I always try to bring a lot of enthusiasm to my job, you know? Being in sales, you kind of have to be "on" all the time, and I really love what I do, so getting motivated isn't really a problem for me. 

I mean, sure, sometimes by Friday afternoon I might feel a little worn out, but that's just because I try to put so much effort into my accounts during the week. I think anyone would be a little tired after that! But I bounce right back after a good night's sleep. I definitely don't just sit around feeling exhausted for no reason, and I always push myself to get things done. 

I hope that's what you were looking for? I just want to make sure I'm giving you a clear picture of how I'm doing. Is it okay that I'm usually pretty energetic?
Have you ever had trouble finishing tasks because your mind wandered, even when you weren’t distracted by other people or external things?

Um... my mind wandering? Well... I mean, I really try my hardest to stay focused, especially because my clients deserve my full attention. But... I guess, maybe sometimes? 

Like, if we're in one of those really long strategy meetings, or if I'm reading a really dense client brief... I always start out super focused, taking notes and everything! But then, after a few minutes, I'll kind of... realize I've been staring at the exact same slide or the same paragraph for a while. And I'll have absolutely no idea what the last point was. 

But I always try to catch myself and jump right back in! I don't want anyone to think I don't care about the presentation. I think it just happens because my brain is trying to process so many great ideas for the client all at once, you know? That's not too terrible, is it? I really hope it just means I'm a creative thinker. Does that sound like a normal thing to happen during long meetings?
Can you tell me if there are specific tasks at work that you find especially difficult to finish because your mind wanders or you feel restless, even when you’re trying your hardest to stay focused?

Um... specific tasks? Well, I mean, I always try really hard to get everything done for my clients, because they're so important to me. But... I guess maybe sometimes the... the very end of things can be a little tricky? 

Like, I'll put so much energy into getting a proposal together, or updating all the client details in the CRM system. I'll get all the hard parts done, you know? The creative stuff, the numbers... all of that is usually mostly finished. But then... um... sometimes I might just... forget to do the very last little step. 

Like, I might leave the final version sitting in my drafts instead of actually hitting send, or I'll forget to log the follow-up date in the system. Even though I fully meant to do it! It's just that my brain is already jumping ahead to the next big project or the next client I want to help. 

But it's just little things like that, and I almost always catch it eventually! I really do try my best to be thorough. I hope that doesn't make me sound careless? I just get so excited about moving forward with the work. Is it normal to sometimes overlook those tiny final details when you're really busy?
As a child, did you have trouble staying seated or focusing during structured family activities, like religious services, meals at a restaurant, or long car trips?

Um... as a child? Well, I always tried really hard to be good for my parents during things like long car rides or dinners out. I definitely didn't want to be a bother to anyone! But... I guess I did have a whole lot of energy back then, too. 

I actually remember this starting way before high school. Like, back in elementary school? It wasn't just at home, it was at school, too. My teachers always wrote really nice things on my report cards, saying I was a bright student and everything! But... um... they would also mention that I rushed through my work a little bit, or that I talked out of turn sometimes. I just got so excited to participate and share the answers, you know? 

And... well, I guess sometimes I would forget my homework, or my desk would get a little messy, just stuffed with half-finished papers. I think it was just because I was so eager to move on to the next fun activity! I really hope that just means I was an enthusiastic kid? A lot of children are a little wiggly and scattered like that when they're young, right? I always meant well, I promise!

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient experiences symptoms of inattention or hyperactivity/impulsivity that are not captured in the work setting or childhood history, which could support a diagnosis of ADHD (F90.0) over adjustment disorder (F43.2) or mild depressive episode (F32.0).

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient experiences symptoms of inattention or hyperactivity-impulsivity that are impairing their work performance, while ruling out other conditions like Adjustment Disorder or Mild Depressive Symptoms.

inference.note: The patient's symptoms of restlessness, difficulty staying seated during long meetings, trouble focusing on tasks, and a history of similar behaviors in childhood (e.g., report card comments about rushing through work, talking out of turn, forgetfulness, and a messy desk) strongly support a diagnosis of ADHD, predominantly inattentive presentation. There is no evidence of significant mood symptoms to support F32.0, and no clear pattern of prolonged stress response or maladaptive coping to support F43.2. Symptoms appear to be consistent with F90.0, and no additional differential is needed at this time.
